clue.text: Broadcasting channel failed to answer

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a duct is a channel or conduit

explanation.surface: A TV channel that went off the air when it should have been on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' looks like it belongs with 'channel' as television; it signals that DUCT is heard, sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to avoid or evade it, so the past tense fits a failure to reply.

clue.text: Depressing quality of extremely deplorable town (not Stoke)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters
in the brackets, it says this part is to be left off the town

parts.note: Basingstoke is a town in Hampshire, England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim town with a dismal character, explicitly not Stoke-on-Trent.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not Stoke)' looks like a parenthetical aside; it removes STOKE from BASINGSTOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Debasing means lowering in quality or value, as with debased coinage.

clue.text: Bright red, about to drink in one hostelry and another

indicators.note: the word for about takes in the hostelry, as if drinking it

parts.note: ca, from circa, means about
an inn is a hostelry
a bar is another drinking place

explanation.surface: Someone red-faced, about to have a drink in one pub and then another.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral, mercury sulphide, gives a vivid scarlet pigment, vermilion.

clue.text: On 'orse, what man did wear

parts.note: a man is he, and the dropped aitch of 'orse tells you to drop it here too, giving 'e
someone on a horse rode it

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch question about what a man wore on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing h of 'orse tells you to drop the h from he as well.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear away is to erode, as water wears down rock.

clue.text: The thoughtless take car out, in accordance with recurrent idea

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with 'take' before it, the word for car is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: an automatic action is done without thought
auto is a common short word for a car

explanation.surface: Careless people take a car out for a spin, following some recurring notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... out' is the removal signal around 'car'; 'thoughtless' means done by reflex, not careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thematic relates to a theme, a recurring idea running through a work.

clue.text: No end of break in playing on the sea, typically Elizabethan arrangement

indicators.note: the phrase for the break loses its final letter

parts.note: half-time is the break in the middle of a match
the Bering Sea lies between Alaska and Siberia

explanation.surface: An endless interval in a performance at sea, laid out in Elizabethan fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed timber framing filled with plaster is the characteristic look of Tudor buildings.

clue.text: Sort of winner is still made to struggle

indicators.note: the letters are made to struggle, thrashing into a new order

explanation.surface: A competitor who wins is nonetheless forced to fight hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal recipient, such as an Olympic gold winner, is one kind of victor.

clue.text: Armoured vehicle shortly suppresses revolutionary rising, without exception

indicators.note: the shortened vehicle sits on top of the other piece, holding it down inside
shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a tank is an armoured vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: Mao Zedong led the Chinese communist revolution

explanation.surface: A tank crushes an uprising, sparing nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the vehicle; 'rising' turns the revolutionary's name upward, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means every single one, all without any dissent.

clue.text: In a comparison of sides, wrong for runner to go round

indicators.note: the runner's name goes round the word for wrong

parts.note: Sebastian Coe is a famous British middle-distance runner
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: When comparing teams, a mistake made a runner go the long way round.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry this function is the ratio of adjacent side to hypotenuse in a right-angled triangle.

clue.text: Singer acquired good piece of drum kit

indicators.note: the singer's name takes in another letter, as if acquiring it

parts.note: Bono is the lead singer of U2

explanation.surface: A vocalist picks up a decent bit of percussion equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bongos are small hand drums, often found in a percussion setup.

clue.text: Youth announces panto is to be held, but not at home

indicators.note: the shortened pantomime title is held inside the word for announces

parts.note: to announce is to say, giving says

indicators.note: with 'but' it removes the letters for at home from the panto title

parts.note: Aladdin is a classic British Christmas pantomime
in is a common crossword word for at home

explanation.surface: A young person declares the pantomime will go ahead, but at a venue away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a comic family stage show staged at Christmas in Britain; 'but not at home' trims the title before 'is to be held' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days means the time of youthful inexperience, a phrase from Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Drug pusher who acknowledges no limits?

definitions.meaning: a trader in amphetamine, speed being slang for that drug
a driver who ignores speed limits

explanation.surface: A dealer in narcotics who recognises no boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' are speed limits on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for someone who loves driving fast, and literally a seller of the drug speed.

clue.text: Transport once set off right to the house

parts.note: a stage, short for stagecoach, was a form of transport in the past
having set off, one has left

explanation.surface: An old coach departed, heading right towards the home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'house' is the theatre audience: the actor's left side of the stage is on the audience's right.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage directions are given from the actor's view, so this side is the audience's right.

clue.text: Discover original of really thin walls

indicators.note: the word for thin surrounds the letter like walls

parts.note: lean means thin

indicators.note: the original of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Find out what originally lay behind really flimsy walls.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something is to find it out or come to know it.

clue.text: Close to swearing?

parts.note: an expression meaning almost, with a mild oath in it, so it is close and also verges on cursing

explanation.surface: Someone is on the brink of letting out a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means 'very nearly' and contains a mild oath, so it is both close and near swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal British idiom means almost exactly, with the euphemistic oath giving it a sweary edge.

clue.text: Past bearing boy, accepting an uplifting employment

indicators.note: the boy's name takes in the other letters

parts.note: Adam is a boy's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting turns the short word upwards

parts.note: use means employment of something

explanation.surface: Beyond endurance: a lad takes on a cheering job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns only 'an' upward in this down clue; 'Past bearing' means beyond what can be borne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means to a sickening degree, beyond what can be endured.

clue.text: Ignores a possible fix

indicators.note: a possible version of the letters is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: A potential remedy is overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix an event is to arrange or set it up.

clue.text: Party of women succeeded replacing husband for a week

indicators.note: one letter is swapped for another in the party

parts.note: a hen night is a party for a bride-to-be and her female friends
S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A ladies' night out took over from the husband for a week.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word, from seven nights, means a period of seven days.

clue.text: Ideal sort of loan for flat

definitions.meaning: a loan charging nothing extra for borrowing is the best kind
flat means dull, lacking anything engaging

explanation.surface: Perfect kind of borrowing to buy an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home to buy; it means dull, free of anything to engage attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Read one way the term is a charge-free loan; read another, it is something devoid of appeal.

clue.text: Horse swallows black stone

indicators.note: the horse takes the letters for black inside it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
BL is an abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A horse gulps down a dark pebble.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard metamorphic rock is a classic building and carving stone.

clue.text: Wrapper of novel — it's horrible!

parts.note: Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling
the exclamation oh no, written O NO

explanation.surface: A reader reacts with dismay to a book's jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrapper' looks like a book jacket; it is a loose robe.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese robe is wrapped around the body and tied with a sash.

clue.text: Going, going … what am I bid?

definitions.text: Going, going … what am I bid?

parts.words: Going, going … what am I bid?
parts.note: the auctioneer's patter conceals a farewell: when going one bids a goodbye

explanation.surface: An auctioneer calls for bids as the hammer is about to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The bidding is a red herring: one 'bids' farewell, and the thing bid when going is this French goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word of farewell is what one says or bids when departing.

clue.text: Leader's symbol of office that is with something pink inside

definitions.note: read as leader is, the 's linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the following letters are placed within the word for a symbol of office

parts.note: a mayor's chain is a badge of office
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
the Financial Times, abbreviated FT, is printed on pink paper

explanation.surface: A leader's regalia includes something pink tucked in.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan head or tribal chief is a leader of a people.

clue.text: He held the greatest ring not to be enough

parts.note: in to and fro, fro is the opposite direction of to
to do is to suffice, as in that will do

explanation.surface: A boxer held the title but it did not suffice.
explanation.walkthrough: The hobbit in The Lord of the Rings carried the One Ring; 'ring' is not a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's hobbit hero was the bearer of the One Ring, the most powerful of all.

clue.text: Loudly disapprove of sugary confection that may come back on you

definitions.text: that may come back on you

indicators.note: said loudly, the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: boo is a jeer of disapproval and meringue a sugary confection

explanation.surface: Jeer at a sweet dessert, which might backfire on you.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved throwing stick returns to the thrower; figuratively, something that rebounds.

clue.text: Down — why unable to fly?

definitions.meaning: being down money means being in debt to someone
a bird with zero wings cannot fly, so the reason is '...', with O as nought

explanation.surface: Feeling low, and asking why one cannot take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like feathers or sadness; it means in debt. The second part reads the answer as O (nought) WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone owing money is down by that amount, in arrears.

clue.text: War crime perhaps men committed in hatred

indicators.note: the men are put inside the word for hatred, as if committed to an institution

parts.note: enmity is hostility or hatred
OR, other ranks, stands for soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An atrocity in wartime, carried out by soldiers driven by hatred.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means great wickedness, or an outrageous act, so a war crime is an example.

clue.text: Very fast stretch of water

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A channel whose water flows very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SOLENT is the strait between the Isle of Wight and the English mainland; 'fast' means abstinence, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The strait separating the Isle of Wight from Hampshire is a named stretch of sea.
